help.title: How to play
help.controls: Tap a piece and then a target square, or drag it. With the keyboard: arrow keys pick a square, Enter selects a piece and a move, Escape cancels the selection.
help.rules: Castling is a king's move of two squares. When a pawn promotes, choose the new piece. The goal is to checkmate your opponent's king.
help.clock: The clocks keep running if the connection drops. You can claim a draw by threefold repetition or the 50-move rule when the button appears.

claim.title: This move lets you claim a draw
claim.description: You can end the game in a draw under the repetition or 50-move rule, or keep playing.

confirm.resignDescription: Your opponent gets the win. After that, you can offer a rematch.

rules.title: Rules
rules.telephone: Everyone writes a phrase, the next player draws it, and the one after that describes the drawing. You only see the previous step. At the end, the host shows all the stories.
rules.classic: Take turns choosing and drawing a word — no letters or numbers. Everyone else types guesses. The faster you guess, the more points you get. The artist scores for every correct guess.
rules.voice: The voice chat keeps going. Don't say the word out loud.

headline.telephone: One phrase. A dozen unexpected twists.
headline.classic: Can you get it without words?

intro.telephone: Pass drawings and descriptions around the circle, then see together what the first idea turned into.
intro.classic: One person draws, everyone else guesses. Even the strangest scribbles can win the game.

lobby.telephoneTiming: 45 seconds per phrase, 90 seconds per drawing. Everyone takes part in every story.
